The numbers 1, 2, ..., 2100 are written on a board. Every second, Mark takes two numbers on the board, \( a \) and \( b \), erases them, and replaces them with \( \gcd(a, b) \) and \( \operatorname{lcm}(a, b) \). Mark stops once any move he makes will not change the numbers written on the board. Compute the number of divisors of the 2026th smallest positive integer written on the board when he finishes.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

Let \(N=2100\). For a prime \(p\), write \(v_p(n)\) for the exponent of \(p\) in \(n\).

When Mark replaces \((a,b)\) by \((\gcd(a,b),\operatorname{lcm}(a,b))\), for each prime \(p\) the two exponents \(v_p(a),v_p(b)\) are replaced by their minimum and maximum. Hence, for every prime \(p\), the multiset of \(p\)-exponents on the board is invariant.

A move changes the board exactly when the chosen two numbers are not comparable by divisibility. The process terminates at a board where every pair of numbers is comparable, so the board is a divisibility chain. Because each prime-exponent multiset is fixed, in the final chain the \(i\)-th smallest number must have, for each prime \(p\), the \(i\)-th smallest \(p\)-exponent from the numbers \(1,2,\dots,2100\).

For a prime \(p\), the number of integers \(n\le 2100\) with \(v_p(n)\ge r\) is
\[
\left\lfloor \frac{2100}{p^r}\right\rfloor.
\]
The 2026th smallest \(p\)-exponent is the largest \(r\ge 0\) such that at least \(2100-2026+1=75\) integers have exponent at least \(r\). Thus
\[
\left\lfloor \frac{2100}{p^r}\right\rfloor \ge 75
\iff p^r \le \frac{2100}{75}=28.
\]
So the exponent of \(p\) in the 2026th final number is \(\lfloor \log_p 28\rfloor\).

The primes \(\le 28\) are
\[
2,3,5,7,11,13,17,19,23.
\]
Their exponents are:
\[
2^4=16,\quad 3^3=27,\quad 5^2=25,
\]
and each of \(7,11,13,17,19,23\) appears to the first power. All other primes have exponent \(0\).

Therefore the 2026th smallest final number has prime factorization
\[
2^4\cdot 3^3\cdot 5^2\cdot 7\cdot 11\cdot 13\cdot 17\cdot 19\cdot 23.
\]
Its number of positive divisors is
\[
(4+1)(3+1)(2+1)(1+1)^6
=5\cdot 4\cdot 3\cdot 2^6
=3840.
\]

\[
\boxed{3840}
\]
